Two design points worth keeping:
- Bound is EXEMPLAR_PAIR_ENDS_PER_SIDE = 6 ENDS PER SIDE (<=36 pairs), not a top-N list of pairs. PROVEN UNFIXABLE ON THIS SIGNAL, which is why it closes rather than iterating: d_S is maximal when the two ankles are furthest apart vertically, which with S planted is the CONTRALATERAL FOOT'S SWING APEX — a real gait event, not touchdown. Sweeping the fixture's apex phase, the emitted lag tracks it one for one from 1 to 11 frames (0.04-0.44s), a range WIDER THAN A WHOLE STANCE PHASE. No constant offset can be right for every runner. CLOSED AS SUPERSEDED — NOT BUILT. Every piece of evidence this ticket was filed on has since been explained by a root cause with its own ticket, and adding the confidence term it asked for would now mask a bug we are already fixing.

The ticket asked that metrics reporting High confidence on run-to-run-unstable values be demoted. Its three evidence items, tracked to conclusion:

1. multiperson overstriding, filed as 0.0114-0.0542 (4.8x spread) at confidence 0.958-1.000.
   DID NOT REPRODUCE. The 2026-08-29 baseline (same harness that verified every ticket in this batch, 3 trials) returned 0.0113843 FLAT across all three trials, with detectedFrames flat at 127 (filed as 103-127) and evidence coverage flat at 4/3. The spread was session-specific.

2. demo1 verticalRatio, filed as 0.0524-0.0682 (30% spread) at confidence 0.727.
   GONE, twice over. strides-dy8 made the metric null (its stride denominator spanned one step, not one stride). strides-da8 then brought it back at 0.0353937 with a 0.006% spread across 3 trials — DETERMINISTIC. The instability was the stride-pairing defect, not a confidence-calibration gap.

3. The within-run dispersion framing I substituted when 1 and 2 evaporated (demo1 overstriding MAD 0.2403 vs median 0.2266).
   ROOT-CAUSED to strides-da8's phase residual, with arithmetic I did not have when I wrote the PM decision on this ticket. During stance the planted foot is fixed in the image while the hip advances, so overstriding's ratio falls at ~3.7 torso lengths/second on this clip; the 0.30s within-trial phase scatter moves the ratio by of order a whole torso length — several times the entire reported range. Dispersion is a SYMPTOM. It should collapse if and only if the phase is fixed, which is filed as the hip-bounce-inflection follow-up.

WHY NOT BUILD IT ANYWAY. A dispersion-based confidence penalty added now would (a) treat a symptom whose cause is understood and scheduled, (b) be calibrated against spreads that will change when the phase lands, and (c) put an uncalibrated coefficient into a user-visible score on a three-clip evidence base — which is exactly what this ticket's own DESIGN field, cadence.ts's doc on the absent footstrike-agreement caveat, and derive-area-floor-from-4k-measurement all independently rejected.

WHAT REMAINS TRUE AND IS TRACKED ELSEWHERE: demo1 overstriding (73% spread) and footStrikePattern (78% spread) currently report High confidence. That is real and user-visible. It is the acceptance criterion of the hip-bounce-inflection follow-up, which requires exactly that those spreads collapse — so the concern is not dropped, it is attached to its cause.

REOPEN THIS if the phase fix lands and High-confidence metrics remain run-to-run unstable. At that point the dispersion would be irreducible rather than a symptom, and a confidence term would be the right answer with real evidence behind it.
